channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 1º de maio
item.description: The JCaesar cartoon published on May 1st, 2026 makes political reference to Congress, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and Senator Davi Alcolumbre, using humor to comment on Brazil's political situation. The illustration, published by VEJA, maintains the satirical tone characteristic of the artist, focusing on central figures of national power.

item.title: “Lula acabou, está nocauteado”, diz Caiado sobre rejeição a Messias
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado stated that the Senate's rejection of Lula's nominee Jorge Messias to the STF marks the end of Lula's government, attributing the outcome to the president's arrogance and disconnection from current politics. Caiado called the vote the first such defeat since 1894 and said it exposes Lula's political isolation, also criticizing Messias for lacking the necessary legal notoriety for the position.

item.title: O que a rejeição de Messias diz sobre o STF e o futuro das indicações
item.description: The Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF in 2025 marks a historic event, being the first time since the 1988 Constitution that a presidential nominee to the Federal Supreme Court was blocked by the Legislature, ending a 132-year streak without rejections. The defeat reflects the increasing politicization of the nomination process, with resistance from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and mobilization by Bolsonarist opposition, and occurs in a sensitive electoral context, as Lula sought to appeal to evangelical voters through Messias, a member of the Baptist Christian Church.

item.title: Bolsonaro é internado para cirurgia no ombro em hospital de Brasília
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro was admitted to DF Star Hospital in Brasília for shoulder surgery, authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The procedure aims to repair the rotator cuff and associated lesions, following clinical improvement from bilateral pneumonia. Bolsonaro has been under temporary humanitarian house arrest since March 27, with an initial 90-day period, due to his health condition.

item.title: Um ano depois, Lula ainda não aprovou o fim da 6 X 1
item.description: One year after announcing the deepening of the debate on reducing the workweek, President Lula has still not approved the end of the 6X1 work schedule, despite listing it as a government priority. The executive’s proposal aims to cut the weekly workload from 44 to 40 hours with two days off (5X2), without wage reduction, while three related PECs remain pending in Congress. The administration favors its own bill due to the presidential veto power, unlike constitutional amendments, which bypass presidential sanction — a issue gaining electoral traction as Lula’s popularity declines and Flávio Bolsonaro rises in the polls.

item.title: Lula falta a atos de 1º de Maio pelo 2º ano seguido para evitar vexame
item.description: President Lula skipped the May Day rallies for the second year in a row to avoid political embarrassment following setbacks like Jorge Messias' Senate defeat. Instead, he delivered a prerecorded national address defending reduced working hours and announcing the second phase of the Desenrola debt-relief program. Government officials including Luiz Marinho, Leonardo Barchini, Fernando Haddad, and Simone Tebet attended the events, with the main protest agenda focused on ending the 6x1 work schedule.

item.title: PSB será protagonista da reestruturação da esquerda no pós-Lula, diz ministro
item.description: Paulo Pereira, Minister of Entrepreneurship and a key PSB figure, says the party aims to credential itself in the elections to become a protagonist of the left in the 'post-Lula' era. He emphasizes the PSB's ambition to play a central role in restructuring the Brazilian left after the current administration.

item.title: Centrão e bolsonarismo exageram na medida e dão munição a contra-ataque
item.description: Centrists and Bolsonarists are overreaching in their efforts to weaken Lula's government, creating openings for counterattacks. This aggressive strategy not only strengthens the left-wing opposition but also risks fracturing the right-wing coalition centered around Flávio Bolsonaro, as even his allies worry about the excessive tone of the attacks.

item.title: A fake news que abalou um presidenciável em 1921 e as eleições de 2026
item.description: The proximity of the 2026 elections raises concerns about the likely impact of disinformation, which is being deployed at scale to undermine candidates and the electoral system itself. False narratives, such as the one that destabilized a presidential candidate in 1921, remain potent tools for manipulating public opinion. Vigilance and fact-checking are essential to safeguard the integrity of the vote.

item.title: Rejeição de Messias no Senado afeta campanha de Lula? Especialistas opinam
item.description: The Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF is not expected to significantly affect President Lula's voting intentions, according to political scientists interviewed by UOL. The decision is seen as an isolated judicial episode with little direct influence on the 2026 electoral campaign.

item.title: Imprensa francesa destaca revés de Lula após derrubada de veto que beneficia Bolsonaro
item.description: French media highlighted the setback for Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva after Congress overturned his veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which reduced the sentence of former President Jair Bolsonaro, convicted to 27 years for attempted coup. The decision, made on Thursday (30), comes six months ahead of the 2026 elections, in which Lula seeks a fourth term at age 80.

item.title: Derrota histórica de Messias eleva tensão política e enfraquece candidatura de Lula
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Federal Court by the Senate in a 42-34 vote marks the first historic defeat of a Lula administration nominee to the court in over a century, exposing political fragility and weakening the Workers' Party’s 2026 re-election bid. The outcome, described as surprising in scale, was amplified by a leaked audio of Senate President Davi Alcolumbre predicting the loss by eight votes to government leader Jaques Wagner, revealing clear opposition coordination. Lula sought to downplay the setback, but the episode deepened Executive-Legislative tensions, created a vacancy on the Court, and raised doubts about his ability to govern with allied support.

item.title: Fortes emoções
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro presents himself as a 'project of God' and a presidential candidate for the PL, claiming his mission is divine and part of a plan to save souls and honor God in Brazil. His campaign emphasizes keywords like family, education, and entrepreneurship, attempting to replace traditional slogans with religious rhetoric. Despite his famous surname and strong anti-Lula support in regions like Sinop, he lacks a distinct identity, being widely seen only as Jair Bolsonaro’s son, with little personal recognition or concrete policy proposals among voters.

item.title: Marcos Pereira, presidente do Republicanos: “Atacar o STF é lamentável”
item.description: Marcos Pereira, president of the Republicans party, condemned the politicization of Supreme Court minister impeachments as lamentable, advocating for harmony among the branches of government and denying direct support for Lula in the 2026 election. While denying the existence of the 'Centrão,' he signaled conditional support for Flávio Bolsonaro, contingent on gestures favoring Republican candidates in state races. As a jurist, he attributes judicialization of politics to party inaction and argues that STF conduct regulation should be debated internally by the Court.

item.title: Banco Master: partidos e políticos trocam farpas no rastro das revelações que ainda podem surgir
item.description: The Banco Master, involved in fraud exceeding 50 billion reais, is linked to corruption suspicions involving Bolsonaro government politicians, including donations from Fabiano Zettel, the bank owner's brother-in-law, to Bolsonaro and Tarcísio de Freitas campaigns. The PT used a video at its national congress to associate Flávio Bolsonaro with the scheme, calling him 'Bolsonaro's most corrupt son' and implying he bought a Brasília mansion with Master funds. The case is expected to be central in the 2026 electoral campaign, particularly in the presidential and São Paulo gubernatorial races.

item.title: Redução de pena para os golpistas do 8 de janeiro é crime continuado
item.description: Congress overturned Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Bill, reducing penalties for the January 8, 2023 coup plotters. The move was celebrated by Bolsonarist lawmakers, though subject to future Supreme Court review. The defeat marks the first rejection of an STF nomination in 132 years and raises concerns about weakening democratic institutions.

item.title: Longe dos estereótipos: pesquisas exclusivas mostram retrato fiel dos conservadores brasileiros
item.description: A Vetor Arrow survey revealed that Brazilian conservatives, representing 53% of the population per Quaest, are not a monolith but five distinct tribes — including 'light antifeminists', 'agronejo', 'pentecostal pop', and 'workers' — who uphold traditional values while engaging with modernity. This diversity challenges stereotypes of machismo, authoritarianism, and state hostility, revealing a more nuanced and adaptable conservatism essential to understanding the 2026 electorate.

item.title: Acordo, atrito ou ruptura
item.description: The Senate's rejection of President Lula's nominee Jorge Messias to the STF marks an unprecedented moment in Brazilian history, reflecting a deep institutional crisis where the branches of government are imbalanced and the Lula administration appears weakened. The text notes that historically, Brazilian crises have been resolved through agreements, frictions, or ruptures — as in 1930, 1945, 1964, 1985, and the presidential impeachments — suggesting the current impasse may follow a similar path, with the president bearing the political cost. Lula could frame the defeat as resistance to undue pressure, but may lack the energy to sustain such a confrontation, leaving the country on an uncertain trajectory between negotiation, tension, or institutional rupture.

item.title: ‘O PT cometeu um erro ao não assinar a CPI do Master’, diz Edinho Silva, presidente do partido
item.description: Edinho Silva, president of the Workers' Party (PT), admitted the party made a mistake by not signing the request to install the CPI investigating Banco Master, stating it should have led the inquiry given the seriousness of the allegations. He criticized recent government defeats in Congress, including the rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court and the overturning of Lula's veto on a bill reducing sentences for those involved in the January 8 attacks, declaring Brazil's political model 'totally destroyed'.

item.title: Bastidores: Base de Lula vê novo relator da escala 6x1 com boa relação com o governo
item.description: Lula’s base expressed satisfaction with the appointment of Deputy Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA) as rapporteur of the special committee on the PEC to end the 6x1 work scale, citing his good relations with the government and centrist profile. Despite the approval, government allies deny that the Planalto proposed his name, attributing the choice to Chamber President Hugo Motta, who favors centrist figures in high-tension issues. The Centrão, however, views Prates as more left-leaning than former rapporteur Paulo Azi and questions his ability to handle intense pressures due to his inexperience as a first-term lawmaker.

item.title: O que o STF fará após a derrubada dos vetos ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Congress overturned President Lula's vetoes on the Dosimetria bill, voting 318-144 in the Chamber and 49-24 in the Senate, reducing sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, including Bolsonaro. Bolsonarist lawmakers celebrated and expect the Supreme Court not to reverse the decision, claiming the bill was pre-negotiated with STF's majority-aligned ministers. The vote came one day after the Senate rejected Jorge Messias' nomination to the Court.

item.title: Bolsonarismo segue roteiro de partido de Trump ao tentar adiar indicação do STF para 2027
item.description: Following the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), bolsonarist opposition has advocated delaying the filling of Luís Roberto Barroso's vacancy until after the 2026 presidential election, in 2027, mirroring the 2016 Republican strategy in the U.S. that blocked Barack Obama's nomination of Merrick Garland to the Supreme Court during an election year.

item.title: Aliados de Lula no Congresso se dividem sobre reação do governo após derrotas, e centrão fala em risco de tensionamento
item.description: Lula's allies in Congress are divided over the government's response following the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF. Some advocate a confrontational stance toward Congress, claiming it strengthens popular support, while others warn that heightened tensions in an election year could jeopardize Lula's re-election and block key executive priorities.

item.title: Análise: derrota histórica com rejeição de Messias provoca tiroteio entre governistas
item.description: The historic rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court triggered an internal crisis in Lula's government, with accusations of negligence and betrayal aimed at allies such as Jaques Wagner, José Guimarães, and Wellington Lima. Prominent senators, despite denying they voted against him, are blamed for the defeat, revealing weaknesses in the government's political articulation. It remains unclear whether Lula will submit a new nominee for the vacancy.

item.title: Derrota em dose dupla: o governo Lula virou "refém" do Congresso?
item.description: Within 24 hours, the Lula government suffered two significant defeats in Congress: the rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF, the first since 1892, and the overturning of the veto on the Dosimetria Bill, which reduces sentences for those convicted of the January 8 acts, directly benefiting Jair Bolsonaro. These events highlight the weakness of the government’s congressional base and the growing strength of the bolsonarist opposition.

item.title: Uma agenda para o Brasil
item.description: The author, a political analyst, announces his intention to contribute to the debate on Brazil’s future in 2026 through a policy agenda, as he has done in previous electoral cycles. The article, exclusive to subscribers, will be published biweekly in his column starting in 2026. Full access requires registration via the provided link.

item.title: Jogo Político: Flávio Bolsonaro ensaia rifar Cláudio Castro e lançar a mãe para o Senado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is considering replacing Cláudio Castro as the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial candidate in 2026 and launching his mother, Rosangela Bolsonaro, as a Senate candidate. The move aims to consolidate the Bolsonarist legacy in the state, despite internal resistance and Castro's current popularity.

item.title: Lula deve encerrar mandato sem viabilizar parte das promessas voltadas aos trabalhadores
item.description: President Lula will end his third term without fulfilling key worker promises, such as new labor legislation and app-based work regulation, despite progress on minimum wage, income tax exemption, and gender pay equity. His absence from May Day events sparked tensions with union centrals, which, nevertheless, plan to support his 2026 re-election. Union leaders praise some government actions but criticize the lack of effort to revise the 2017 labor reform to strengthen union funding.

item.title: 'Bode expiatório' e 'ilações mentirosas': busca do Planalto por traições sobre Messias estremece relação com aliados
item.description: The defeat of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Court has led the Lula government to suspect betrayals within its allied base, particularly in the MDB and PP parties. Party leaders have denied the accusations, calling them 'scapegoating' and 'false claims', arguing the government is shifting blame for the loss. Senate President Davi Alcolumbre's role in consolidating opposition to the nomination is seen as pivotal.

item.title: Saiba tudo sobre a nova derrota do governo que abre caminho para reduzir pena de Bolsonaro
item.description: Congress overturned President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's veto on the Dosimetria Bill, which changes sentencing rules and could reduce penalties for those involved in the January 8 attacks. The move marks another setback for the Lula government, coming just one day after the rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Court. Former President Jair Bolsonaro is identified as the potential main beneficiary of this legal change.

item.title: Sindicatos mineiros promovem atos de 1º de Maio pelo fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Mineiro unions are organizing May Day demonstrations in Belo Horizonte to demand the end of the 6x1 work schedule, supporting Bill 1838/2026 and other proposals to reduce working hours. Events include a workers' mass, unified acts at Praça Raul Soares and the Paulo Freire Occupation square, and the Workers' Samba under the Santa Tereza Viaduct. Beyond work hours, the protests address femicide, pejotization, strengthening collective bargaining, and defense of public services, including opposition to the privatization of Copasa.

item.title: Rejeição de Messias respinga na eleição de MG e complica cenário para Lula
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF in the Senate, with 42 votes against and 34 in favor, was a major setback for the Lula government and has sparked distrust around Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB), seen as Lula's Plan A for the Minas Gerais gubernatorial race. Although Pacheco publicly supported Messias, he refused to disclose his vote, fueling suspicions that he may have contributed to the defeat, undermining Lula’s electoral strategy in a key state for 2026.

item.title: Assessor é exonerado após invadir programa ao vivo, xingar e pedir reeleição de Lula
item.description: Parliamentary aide Bernardo Moreira Amado Barros was dismissed after invading the live broadcast of Globonews' Estúdio i, where he shouted an insult and called for Lula's re-election. The incident occurred during an interview with deputies Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB) and Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) regarding the congressional rejection of President Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which would reduce sentences for those involved in the January 8 attacks. The dismissal was signed by Chamber President Hugo Motta and published in the Official Gazette of the Union.

item.title: Trump usa la sentencia del Supremo que cercena los derechos de las minorías para mejorar sus perspectivas electorales
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court's decision weakening the 1965 Voting Rights Act prompted Louisiana to postpone its May primary elections, disrupting the path to November's midterm legislative races. The move is seen as part of Trump's strategy to improve his electoral prospects by diminishing minority representation.

item.title: Rejeição de Messias cria atalho conservador ao Supremo
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias's nomination to the Supreme Court and Davi Alcolumbre's signal that he will not schedule a new nomination before the election give the right an opportunity to build a majority on the STF if they win the 2026 presidential race. This could consolidate a conservative tilt on the Court, influencing rulings on abortion, guns, and identity policies.

item.title: Crise com Alcolumbre coloca em xeque avanço de pautas prioritárias de Lula no Congresso
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF and the overturning of Lula’s veto on the Dosimetria Bill, blamed on Senate President Davi Alcolumbre’s maneuvering, have triggered a crisis threatening the advancement of key government priorities, including the 6x1 workweek reduction and the Security PEC. While allies see electoral momentum to push for shorter workweeks, there is concern that Congress may seize the issue and sidestep the executive’s proposal.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro sobe no salto e mostra que já se considera eleito
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro shows confidence in his candidacy following bolsonarist victories in Congress, including the historic rejection of a Supreme Court nomination and the overturning of Lula’s veto on a bill reducing penalties for coup plotters. The senator, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, positions himself as a central figure in the movement and already acts as if elected for 2026.

item.title: Novo Desenrola: o que já se sabe sobre a renegociação de dívidas que Lula apresenta na segunda
item.description: President Lula announced on national radio and TV the creation of the 'New Desenrola Brasil', a debt renegotiation program to be presented on Monday. The initiative aims to assist indebted Brazilians, though specific operational details have not yet been disclosed. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Seis partidos na Câmara e cinco no Senado votaram 100% a favor da redução da pena dos condenados pelo 8 de janeiro
item.description: Congress overturned President Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Bill, reducing sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, including Jair Bolsonaro. In the Chamber, 318 deputies voted to overturn the veto, with six parties voting unanimously in favor (PL, PSDB, Novo, PRD, Cidadania and Missão). In the Senate, 49 senators approved the measure, with five parties unanimously favorable (PL, PSDB, Novo, União Brasil and Avante).

item.title: Após Congresso derrubar veto de Lula, discussão sobre redução de penas deve voltar ao Supremo
item.description: Congress overturned President Lula's veto on a bill reducing sentences for those convicted of coup-related acts, including former President Jair Bolsonaro. The law will now be promulgated and may face review at the Supreme Court. Legal experts argue there are no apparent constitutional flaws, as Congress acted within its legitimate legislative authority.

item.title: Cláudio Castro recorre ao TSE contra inelegibilidade de 8 anos
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) appealed to the TSE against his 8-year ineligibility, imposed for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. His defense claims violations of due process, seeks annulment of the ruling, and requests modified effects to enable his Senate bid in 2026. Former Alerj president Rodrigo Bacellar filed a similar appeal to regain his state deputy seat.

item.title: Após crise com Lula, Alcolumbre deve dar aval a apoio de União e PP a Flávio
item.description: Leaders of the União Progressista federation (União Brasil/PP) believe Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) will not engage in open confrontation with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva following the rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF. They expect Alcolumbre to endorse the support of União and PP for Senator Flávio Dino, opting for negotiation over rupture with the government.

item.title: Sem Lula, esquerda fragmenta atos de 1º de Maio e reforça embate após veto a Messias
item.description: Left-wing movements are organizing fragmented May Day actions to pressure for the end of the 6x1 work scale, following recent defeats of Lula's government in Congress. The mobilization occurs amid internal divisions and reinforces opposition to the veto on Messias, highlighting the fragmentation of the Brazilian left amid growing government weariness.

item.title: Novo Desenrola Brasil terá FGTS, desconto de até 90% e bloqueio de bets: o que Lula anunciou
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced a new phase of the Desenrola Brasil program, offering discounts of up to 90% on credit card, overdraft, revolving credit, personal loan, and FIES debts, along with the ability to withdraw up to 20% of FGTS funds to pay off debt. The initiative includes interest rates as low as 1.99% per month and a one-year ban on online betting platforms for participants, aiming to reduce household indebtedness, which affects 80.4% of Brazilian families.

item.title: Flávio visita Bolsonaro após derrubada do veto à dosimetria
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) visited former President Jair Bolsonaro after Congress overturned Lula’s veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which reduces sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks. Bolsonaro celebrated the decision, which could reduce his sentence from 27 years and 3 months to 20 years and 8 months, also benefiting 849 others. Flávio emphasized his father’s gratitude to loyal lawmakers and highlighted the unity of the bolsonarist base.

item.title: Moraes dá 48 horas para ‘Débora do Batom’ explicar falhas em tornozeleira eletrônica
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes gave Débora Rodrigues dos Santos, known as 'Débora do Batom', 48 hours to explain GPS failures in her electronic ankle monitor. She is serving a 14-year sentence under house arrest since September 2025 for her role in the January 8 coup attempt. The case has become a symbol of Bolsonarist pressure for amnesty for those involved in the attacks on the three branches of government.

item.title: Veto de Lula a projeto que reduz pena de Bolsonaro é derrubado com votos de partidos com ministérios
item.description: President Lula's veto to a bill that would reduce Jair Bolsonaro's sentence was overturned by Congress, with decisive support from centrist parties holding ministries in his government, such as PSD and União Brasil. The vote reveals the fragility of Lula's PT-led coalition amid parliamentary pressures and political bargains.

item.title: Líder do PT diz que base do governo vai recorrer ao STF após derrubada do veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: PT leader Pedro Uczai announced the government base will seek judicial review after Congress overturned Lula’s veto on the dosimetry bill, which reduces sentences for January 8 attackers and benefits Jair Bolsonaro. The veto was overturned following a procedural maneuver by Congress President Davi Alcolumbre to avoid conflict with the Anti-Faction Law. PT critics denounced a 'backroom deal' between opposition and centrals, warning the move could aid criminal faction leaders.

item.title: Imprensa internacional repercute redução de pena de Bolsonaro e destaca relação 'frágil' de Lula com Congresso
item.description: International press highlighted that Brazil's Congress overturned President Lula's veto on a bill reducing sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, benefiting former President Jair Bolsonaro, marking the government's second defeat in 24 hours. Outlets including The Guardian, La Nación, The Washington Post, and El País emphasized that this exposes the fragility of Lula's relationship with a predominantly conservative Congress ahead of the October elections. The potential challenge in the Supreme Court and its electoral implications were widely noted.

item.title: Lula anuncia novo Desenrola para a próxima semana com até 20% do FGTS
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced the launch of the New Desenrola Brasil program for next Monday, offering discounts of up to 90% on debts and allowing the use of up to 20% of the FGTS to settle debts. The program includes a one-year ban on online betting platforms for participants and aims to ease family budgets, particularly for high-cost debts like credit cards and overdrafts. Lula also reiterated the end of the 6x1 work scale as a historic step, proposing a 40-hour workweek with two days off and no salary reduction.
